Sampled-negative metrics can reverse model rankings relative to full-catalog evaluation, even in expectation; easy pair separation therefore cannot establish top-K ranking quality. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) establish this inconsistency; a [2025 study](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) examines sampling reliability through resolution, fidelity, robustness and predictive power. Keep host validation HR@10 unchanged; supplement it with explicitly labeled full-catalog training-prefix audits. Full-catalog ranking still measures recovery of observed interactions, not complete user relevance.

Behavioral testing offers stronger diagnostic grounding than embedding alignment alone. [RecList](https://github.com/RecList/reclist) supports targeted behavioral tests and subgroup analysis; [Does It Look Sequential? (RecSys 2024)](https://github.com/Antondfger/Does-It-Look-Sequential) uses sequence shuffling and finds weak sequential structure in several common datasets. Proposed audit: freeze users, training-prefix cutoffs and next-item targets; exclude targets from input; score eligible catalog items; report HR@10, NDCG@10 and target ranks by training-only popularity strata. Compare intact histories against shuffled nonpadding events, history replacement and last-item-only inputs. Small shuffle effects can reflect weak dataset chronology, so they do not independently prove a model defect.

For probe validation, deliberately inject history-independent scoring and chronology destruction; measure detection sensitivity and false alarms. These are proposed controls, not established benchmark findings. Add fixed lexical competitors retrieved using TF-IDF/BM25 over permitted titles/descriptions, but treat them as unobserved competitors rather than verified negatives: [2024 research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) highlights false-negative risks. Report paired user-bootstrap intervals, subgroup counts, wall time and peak memory. Chunk catalog scoring and count outranking items without sorting; scoring cost scales approximately with audit users × catalog size × feature dimension. Measure coverage/concentration directly before claiming diversity loss.
